title: One Parameter
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to give a function one parameter so the same function can work with different values each time you call it.
learn: Add one parameter in the def line
Use the parameter name inside the function
idea: A parameter is a variable you write inside the parentheses on the def line. An argument is the real value you pass in when you call the function. With one parameter, you can greet Alice and Bob using the same greet function. Only the argument changes.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first call from greet("Alice") to greet("Maya"). Press Run. The first line should say Hello, Maya.

practice.text: Finish greet(name) so it prints a hello using the name. Call it with two different names.
practice.hint: Use the parameter name inside print. For example print("Hello,", name). Add a second greet("...") call with a different name.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Hello,", name) in the function body, then add greet("Alex") on the blank line below greet("Sam").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if greet has a name parameter, prints using that parameter, and is called at least twice with different string arguments.

practice.text: Finish square(n) so it prints n times n. Call it with two different numbers.
practice.hint: Multiply n by itself with n * n (or n ** 2) inside print. Call square twice with different numbers like 3 and 5.
practice.starterTip: Try print(n, "squared is", n * n) inside square, then add square(5) on the blank line below square(3).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if square takes one parameter, prints n*n (or equivalent), and is called at least twice.

quiz.question: In def greet(name):, what is name?
quiz.correct: name sits in the def line, so it is a parameter.
quiz.wrong: Names listed inside the parentheses on the def line are parameters.

quiz.question: What does greet("Ava") pass into the function?
quiz.correct: "Ava" is the argument passed into the name parameter.
quiz.wrong: The value inside the call's parentheses is the argument.

quiz.question: Why use a parameter?

options.text: So one function can work with different inputs

quiz.correct: Parameters let the same function handle many different values.
quiz.wrong: Different arguments in, same function body. That is the point.

project.title: Name Tag Printer
project.desc: Write a function name_tag(name) that prints Hello, my name is and the name. Call it for three different people.
